newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg CEO '96 compensation down from '95.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg CEO '96 compensation down from '95.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Thursday that Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Arnold Langbo received a total compensation package valued at $4,801,970 in 1996.

Included in the figure is salary of $932,500, a bonus of $315,000 and $1,460,070 from exercised stock options; it also includes new options that have an estimated value of $2,094,400, according to the company's 1996 proxy statement.
Langbo's total 1996 figure compares with a 1995 total compensation package valued at $5,786,805.

A year ago, Langbo received a lower salary -- $880,000 -- but a higher bonus of $765,000. Also in 1995, Langbo earned $2,392,805 from exercised options and was granted 150,000 new options then valued at $1,749,000.
Excluding options that Langbo was granted but had not exercised in both years, his 1996 compensation fell to $2,707,570 from $4,037,805 a year ago.

Kellogg said it used the Black-Scholes model to calculate the future value of the 160,000 new options Langbo was granted in 1996. The options, which expire March 15, 2006, carry an exercise price of $77.50 each -- higher than the approximately $66.50 a share at which the stock was trading Thursday.
The company said bonuses for all employees, including Langbo, fell by half because Kellogg reached 80 percent of its 1996 earnings per share target.
Also in the proxy, Kellogg said it had scheduled its annual shareholders meeting for 1300 EDT/1700 GMT April 25 at the W.K. Kellogg Auditorium in Battle Creek.
